title: AI Chatbot Disclosure Check (EU AI Act Article 50)
meta_description: Check whether your website chatbot tells visitors they're talking to an AI, as EU AI Act Article 50 requires. Free check, one-time evidence report.
headline: Does your website chatbot say it's an AI?
subhead: A free check of your public pages for AI chat widgets and a visible AI disclosure, plus an optional dated evidence report for your compliance file.
problem_bullets: Many support tools now switch on AI answers inside the same chat widget, so the duty to disclose can land on you without anyone noticing.
Article 50 of the EU AI Act has applied to AI systems that talk to people since 2 August 2026, including for non-EU companies serving EU users.
A screenshot in someone's inbox is not a record. You need a dated, repeatable check of what visitors actually see.
what_it_will_do: Load the public pages you list (home, contact, help) and detect known chat and voice-AI widgets.
Look for AI-disclosure wording in the launcher, header and first message.
Flag widgets it can't open or read as 'not checked' instead of guessing.
Suggest plain disclosure wording and where it usually goes for your chat vendor.

faqs.q: Is this legal advice?
faqs.a: No. It records what your public pages show and suggests wording. For a legal view of your obligations, ask a qualified adviser.

faqs.q: Does it apply if a human answers our chat?
faqs.a: Article 50(1) is about AI systems that interact with people. If only humans answer, it doesn't bite, but check whether your vendor's AI mode is on.

faqs.q: Can it see logged-in areas or what the bot says later?
faqs.a: No. It checks public pages and the first visible message only, and it says so in the report.

faqs.q: Is it a subscription?
faqs.a: No. The planned report is a one-time payment per site. Re-checks would be priced separately.

title: MCP Server Security Report for Remote Servers
meta_description: Free security check for your remote MCP server: auth, OAuth metadata, transport and risky tool definitions. Optional one-time report for security reviews.
headline: A security report for your remote MCP server
subhead: Run a free check on your own MCP endpoint, then get a one-time report you can hand to a customer's security review.
problem_bullets: Enterprise buyers now ask MCP vendors security questions, and a CLI log is not something you can attach to a questionnaire.
The free scanners are CLIs that need local setup, an account token or a paid engine for some checks.
Auth details like the WWW-Authenticate header and OAuth protected-resource metadata are easy to miss and hard to explain later.
what_it_will_do: Check transport and TLS on your remote endpoint (Streamable HTTP or SSE).
Check auth behaviour: 401 responses, WWW-Authenticate, OAuth protected-resource metadata.
Read tool definitions for missing destructive/read-only annotations and instruction-like text inside descriptions.
Check CORS and origin handling on the MCP endpoint.
Show each finding with severity and the spec section it relates to.

faqs.q: Can I scan someone else's server?
faqs.a: The report is meant for servers you own or run. Checks only read what the endpoint exposes publicly or with the auth header you provide.

faqs.q: Is this a penetration test?
faqs.a: No. It's an automated configuration and definition review. It doesn't attempt exploits and doesn't replace a pentest.

faqs.q: Do you store my auth header?
faqs.a: The plan is to use it for that single check and never write it to storage or logs.

faqs.q: Does it cover local stdio servers?
faqs.a: Not at first. It targets remote servers reachable over HTTP.

title: VPAT / ACR Draft Generator for SaaS Products
meta_description: Free accessibility scan of your SaaS pages, then a pre-filled VPAT 2.5 (WCAG) draft with every manual criterion flagged. One-time price, no subscription.
headline: A pre-filled VPAT draft from a scan of your product
subhead: Scan a few pages free. Then get a VPAT 2.5 (WCAG edition) draft filled with what automated checks can show, and a clear list of what still needs a human.
problem_bullets: Buyers in education, government and larger companies ask for a VPAT or Accessibility Conformance Report before they sign.
Consultant-written ACRs commonly cost thousands of dollars, and subscription tools charge every month.
Automated scans cover only part of WCAG, so a 'finished' report from a scanner alone would be misleading.
what_it_will_do: Scan up to 5 public pages against WCAG 2.2 A and AA machine-checkable rules.
Show issues grouped by WCAG criterion with the failing element.
Show which criteria automated testing can't judge.
Estimate how much of the VPAT can be pre-filled from your results.

faqs.q: Is the draft ready to send to a buyer?
faqs.a: Not on its own. It fills what automated checks can show and flags the rest. Someone on your team must review it and complete the manual criteria.

faqs.q: Which VPAT edition?
faqs.a: The plan is the VPAT 2.5 WCAG edition first. Section 508 and EU (EN 301 549) editions may follow if people ask.

faqs.q: How much of WCAG can a scan check?
faqs.a: Only part of it. Things like meaningful alt text and full keyboard flows need a person, and the draft says so.

faqs.q: Is it a subscription?
faqs.a: No. The planned price is one payment per product.

title: GitHub Actions Security Scan and One-Time Fix PR
meta_description: Free scan of your GitHub Actions workflows for unpinned actions, broad token permissions and script injection. Optional one-time fix PR, no subscription.
headline: Find and fix risky GitHub Actions workflows
subhead: A free scan of your workflow files, then an optional pull request that pins actions to commit SHAs and tightens permissions. One-time price, private repos included.
problem_bullets: Actions referenced by a tag can change under you. Pinning to a full commit SHA is the usual fix, and it's tedious by hand.
Many workflows still run with broad GITHUB_TOKEN permissions they never use.
Free hardening tools often cover public repos only, and private-repo plans are usually per-developer subscriptions.
what_it_will_do: Find actions referenced by tag or branch instead of a full commit SHA.
Flag workflows with missing or overly broad permissions blocks.
Flag untrusted event data used inside run: steps (script injection risk).
Flag risky pull_request_target and checkout patterns, and persisted credentials.

faqs.q: Will the fix break my workflows?
faqs.a: Every change arrives as a pull request with an explanation, so your CI runs on it before you merge.

faqs.q: Do you need write access to my code?
faqs.a: The scan only reads workflow files. The planned fix PR would need permission to open a pull request on the repos you choose.

faqs.q: Does it work for private repos?
faqs.a: That's the plan: the same one-time price for public and private repos.

faqs.q: Is this a subscription?
faqs.a: No. You pay once per repo or per 10-repo pack.

title: AI Crawler Access Check and llms.txt Fix Pack
meta_description: Free check of which AI crawlers your robots.txt allows or blocks and whether your llms.txt is valid. Optional one-time fix pack you can paste in.
headline: See which AI crawlers can read your site, then fix it
subhead: A free check of your robots.txt, llms.txt and bot responses, then an optional one-time pack of ready-to-paste files that match the policy you choose.
problem_bullets: One robots.txt line or a CDN bot setting can quietly block the crawlers behind AI answers, or let in ones you meant to block.
llms.txt is new, and small format mistakes make it useless to the tools that read it.
Most monitoring tools are monthly subscriptions when you only need the files done right once.
what_it_will_do: Read robots.txt and resolve, per known AI crawler, whether it's allowed or blocked.
Validate llms.txt and llms-full.txt format and check their links.
Check whether your CDN or firewall returns blocks or challenges to AI crawler user-agents.
Check sitemap and X-Robots-Tag signals that conflict with robots.txt.

faqs.q: Do AI crawlers have to obey robots.txt?
faqs.a: No. Well-behaved crawlers follow it, but it's voluntary. The check shows what your site asks for, not what every bot does.

faqs.q: Should I block AI crawlers?
faqs.a: It depends on your goals. The fix pack lets you choose, for example allow answer crawlers and block training crawlers.

faqs.q: Does llms.txt help?
faqs.a: It's an emerging convention and support varies by tool. The pack makes sure that if you publish one, it's valid.

faqs.q: Is it a subscription?
faqs.a: No. The planned fix pack is a one-time payment per domain.
